paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Wandsworth, including the council's own service, Foster with Wandsworth. The council says it needs carers for children of every age, and especially more foster parents for older children and for brothers and sisters who need to stay together. It pays a weekly fee and allowance, with higher rates for children aged 11 to 18, and says its own carers are offered placements before agency carers.

Its criteria are practical. You must be at least 25, and there is no upper age limit. You can rent or own, be single or in a couple, of any sexuality, and keep pets. You do not need a car or qualifications, and claiming benefits does not rule you out. Each foster child needs a bedroom of their own, although a baby under two can share the carer's room. You can live outside the borough, but within an hour of the child's school. Single carers can work part-time and flexibly; in a couple, one person needs to be at home or working flexibly around school hours. A criminal record is looked at case by case, and the council pays for the enhanced DBS check.

Wandsworth offers short-term, emergency and long-term fostering, Family Link short breaks for disabled children, respite, parent and child, remand and specialist therapeutic care. It says approval takes 16 to 20 weeks on average, and its next monthly information session is on Thursday 19 November 2026 at Wandsworth Town Hall and online.
Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before choosing. If you live near the borough's edge, see the Lambeth, Southwark, Sutton and London pages too.
